skill.name: no-bluff-seo-skill
skill.description: Enforce the No-Bluff SEO/GEO protocol using DataForSEO and SEMRush. Use when generating or modifying any SEO-related copy, claims, or structured data for Synthex or client sites.
skill.summary: Applies evidence, source, and confidence rules to SEO and GEO content.
skill.author: CleanExpo

security_audit.summary: The static analyzer flagged six uses of inline Markdown backticks as Ruby or shell execution. Review of SKILL.md shows these are formatting markers around field names and confidence labels, with no executable commands or command interpolation present.

static_findings.snippet: 3. Attach `source`, `metric_type`, and `confidence_score` to generated SEO insights.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 18 uses Markdown inline code formatting around the table name seo_providers. It is prose documentation, not Ruby or shell backtick execution.
Line 23 uses Markdown inline code formatting around metadata field names. No command is executed and no user-controlled input is evaluated.
Line 44 formats the confidence label high as inline code in documentation. There is no shell context or executable code.
Line 45 formats the confidence label medium as inline code in documentation. This is static Markdown text, not command execution.
Line 46 formats the confidence label low as inline code in documentation. No Ruby, shell, or subprocess behavior is present.
Line 47 formats the confidence label uncertain as inline code in documentation. It does not invoke external commands.

content.value_statement: SEO copy often includes claims that are hard to verify. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to source claims, score confidence, and separate facts from forecasts.
actual_capabilities: Requires SEO claims to cite a source before publication.
Prompts review of keyword metrics from DataForSEO, SEMRush, Google Search Console, Ahrefs, or direct citations.
Adds source, metric type, and confidence score labels to SEO insights.
Separates factual statements, forecasts, and opinions in SEO content.
Guides generation or updates of JSON-LD structured data for supported page types.
Rejects vague vanity claims unless measurable evidence is available.
limitations: It depends on available access to SEO tools and search data.
It does not include executable API integration code.
It cannot verify private rankings, reviews, or metrics without supplied evidence.
It does not replace legal, advertising, or regulatory review.

use_cases.title: Landing Page Claim Review
use_cases.description: Check marketing copy for measurable SEO claims, add sources, and remove unsupported ranking statements.

use_cases.title: Client SEO Audit Preparation
use_cases.description: Create audit notes that show what data was checked, what changed, and how confident each insight is.

use_cases.title: Structured Data Cleanup
use_cases.description: Review product, local business, article, FAQ, and review schema requirements before updating page metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single page draft.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this landing page copy with the No-Bluff SEO protocol. List unsupported claims, required sources, and safer wording.

prompt_templates.title: Score SEO Insights
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate audit of existing keyword or ranking notes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess these SEO insights. Add source, metric type, confidence score, and a short reason for each confidence level.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Structured Data
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced content update for schema markup planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this page type and content. Recommend the appropriate structured data fields and flag any values that need evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Client Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced report quality control before delivery.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this client SEO report for factual claims, forecasts, opinions, vanity metrics, missing sources, and required audit trail notes.

output_examples.input: A landing page says the company is the top-rated provider in its market.
output_examples.output: The claim should be rejected unless current review data supports it. Replace it with a dated rating, review count, source, and confidence label.

output_examples.input: A keyword report includes traffic estimates from multiple tools.
output_examples.output: The report should identify each source, mark direct measurements as high confidence, and label calculated estimates as medium confidence.

output_examples.input: A product page needs search metadata and FAQ schema.
output_examples.output: The page can include product and FAQ structured data when each answer is present on the page and review claims use real reviews.

best_practices: Provide the source data or tool output before asking for claim validation.
Keep dates with statistics so readers know when the evidence was current.
Log checked sources, findings, content changes, and responsible reviewers.
anti_patterns: Do not publish rankings or superlatives without a cited source.
Do not mix facts, forecasts, and opinions in the same unsupported statement.
Do not add review schema unless the reviews are real and visible to users.

faq.question: What does this skill help validate?
faq.answer: It helps validate SEO and GEO claims, keyword insights, structured data, and client-facing audit language.

faq.question: Does it connect to DataForSEO or SEMRush by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides a protocol for using those sources, but access and data must be supplied through available tools.

faq.question: Can it write JSON-LD recommendations?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide structured data choices for product, local business, article, FAQ, and review content.

faq.question: How does confidence scoring work?
faq.answer: Direct measurements are high confidence, calculated values are medium, estimates are low, and weak evidence is uncertain.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should users provide for best results?
faq.answer: Users should provide page copy, keyword data, ranking evidence, source dates, and any required client context.
